name: The Indigo Drop
pitch: One art, one firing, multiplier 1.00: a drop of perfect purity spreads through their sea until everything they throw lands on them.

new.name: One Drop
new.effect: Your first hit leaves 1 % colour. Each pulse colour x (1 + (clean purity - their highest purity) / 50 x spread). That share of their art hits resolves on them, and that share of their ward stops neither you nor them.

new.name: The Clear Line
new.effect: Clean purity is purity -4 per stain: each artifact, pill in effect, art naming another element, or second Way.

new.name: Clean Hands
new.effect: +0.5 % starting colour per empty art slot.

new.name: Bluer Than the Plant
new.effect: At 100 % colour their basic attack turns too.
new.second_home: The Lucky Fool, any self-hit door

new.name: Mordant
new.effect: A cleanse leaves half of the colour.
new.second_home: any status that fears a cleanse

new.name: The Clear Vat
new.effect: Wood sector, sealed by technique, eleven nodes: six Spread acupoints, Steeped, Clean Hands, Mordant, Bluer Than the Plant, One Drop at the far end.

new.name: Clear Vat Canon
new.effect: Main, names only Wood, no bonuses, seals The Clear Vat, gives Falling Drop.

new.name: Falling Drop
new.effect: Qi, Wood, c_art 1.3, cost 0.04, 0.5 s, guarded on the target holding no colour.

questions: Purity 100 buys little against ordinary roots and everything against roots of 85 or more. Is purity meant to be a duel between the few, rather than a stat for everyone?
Enemies always fire when ready. Should an NPC stop casting once its own arts turn on it? The whole build rests on that.
